approach: Add one pure reading check, `check_behavior_test_design`, in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs`. It sits next to `check_code_survey` and reuses `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, `code_surveys`, `names_record_evidence`, `is_record_or_data_deliverable`, `has_phrase` and `straight_lowercase`. It runs on a reading that passed `check_code_survey`, so it only judges readings that already have a crates/ survey. It reads only the reading (survey assumptions, criteria, deliverables), so tests call it on fixture readings and count refusals directly; no model is called. It requires the joined `Code survey:` text to state four things. (a) Entry point, gate order and a stop gate, where the stop gate is an identifier that also appears earlier in the stated order. (b) A reused existing function by identifier, or the explicit words "no existing function". (c) An accepted record kind (`AnyRecord::<Variant>` or an `athena.<kind>/<n>` schema tag, or other `names_record_evidence` evidence), or "no new output", or a typed record with a round-trip test criterion plus a listed deliverable. (d) A direct check that counts calls or events, with no unnegated skip switch or internal-helper read as the measurement in the survey or any criterion. The error names each missing letter (a)-(d) and each contradiction, and gives a one-line template. It is wired as `step!(check_behavior_test_design(reading));` directly after the `check_code_survey` step. Existing fixtures (`SURVEY` in reading.rs tests, three `Code survey:` strings in the corpus) are short and would be refused by the new step before the checks they target, so they are replaced by one complete survey. New corpus cases and unit tests cover each omission, each contradiction and the accepted form. A fixture replay test, and the host's real replay at verification, cover criterion 4. The reader brief's `Code survey` rule line is reworded in place, within its size limits.

decisions.choice: Make the check a lexical function of the reading's `Code survey:` assumptions, criteria and deliverables, with no repository read. 'Contradicts the code' means contradicts a rule this check enforces or contradicts itself: a stop gate missing from the stated order, 'no existing function' beside a reused function, a typed record with no round-trip test, a skip switch or internal-helper read as the measurement.
decisions.reason: `check_code_survey` and the other survey checks read only the Reading (surveys.rs:188, 310, 503), and the gate runs with `repo_files = None` in `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54-55), so a function-level fact cannot be looked up. The accepted reading's Design section names these examples.

rejected.option: Parse the repository's Rust source to confirm each named function exists
rejected.why: The gate and `athena check-reading` have no repository (replay.rs:52-53). It would also make replay results depend on the checkout.

rejected.option: Put the four requirements into a model-judged critic prompt
rejected.why: Out of scope: the plan critic and prompt files are not edited, and the reader prompt has 2 tokens of headroom. The 'mechanism' default asks for a code check, not prose.

decisions.choice: Add a new function `check_behavior_test_design` and a new `step!` line, instead of extending the body of `check_code_survey`.
decisions.reason: `refusing_check` says each new check is one `step!` line, and `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` pins a refusing case per step (checks.rs:513-516, corpus 2905). A separate step also gives the refusal its own rule name in the per-rule counts in `status`, so the replay and status can tell it from the survey-missing refusal.

rejected.why: Its existing tests assert its error text and the record-evidence rule (reading.rs:7071-7167), and the refusal would be counted under the old rule name.

decisions.choice: For (c), reuse `names_record_evidence` as the evidence matcher, add one small helper `names_record_kind` for `AnyRecord::<Variant>` and `athena.<kind>/<n>` tags, and take 'round-trip deliverable' to mean a behavior criterion naming a round-trip identifier plus at least one listed crates/ deliverable. Add no new record kind.
decisions.reason: The accepted reading requires reuse of the matcher. `AnyRecord` and its schema tags are the real accepted kinds (records.rs:1124-1194, `check_record_file` at 1455). Adding no kind keeps `athena-data` and `records/` untouched (out of scope).

rejected.option: Add a public list of accepted kinds to `athena-data` and check named kinds against it
rejected.why: It changes `records.rs`, which would itself trigger the record-evidence rule and is not a listed deliverable.

decisions.choice: Negation-guard the skip-switch and internal-helper phrases: a phrase counts only when no `no`, `not`, `never` or `without` sits within the 3 words before it.
decisions.reason: The request's own wording is 'not a skip switch' and 'not reads of an internal helper', and a good reading will repeat it. `requires_existing_code_section` already guards a negator within 3 words (surveys.rs:1359-1393), so the pattern is established. Without the guard the check would refuse the correct reading.

rejected.option: Refuse on any mention, as `check_history_fixture` does (its doc lists this as a limit, surveys.rs:320)
rejected.why: It would refuse the exact sentence the reader is asked to write.

decisions.choice: Leave `status.rs` and `replay.rs` unchanged and say why in the producer report; update `briefs.rs` only for the check-name list and the rule count if the reader rule line names the new check.
decisions.reason: `status.rs:3908` has `RULE_B` as a test string constant only, and the per-rule stats key on whatever name `refusing_check` returns, so there is nothing to add. `replay()` and `replay_declaration_of` already take a declared share and hold above it plus 5 points (replay.rs:165-308), so the criterion-4 declaration needs no code.

rejected.option: Touch both files to match the deliverables list
rejected.why: An empty edit is churn. Unchanged planned files are reported with a reason (send_back.rs:182), which is a lighter cost.

decisions.choice: Do not raise `READING_RULES_BASELINE_BYTES` or the 3150 cap in briefs.rs. Reword the existing `Code survey` rule line in place (12 rules stay) and drop the reader brief edit if the size test cannot pass.
decisions.reason: Criterion 6 allows the brief line only if the brief test still passes. The section is bounded at 3045 bytes (briefs.rs:3591, 3710-3715) and the test pins 12 lines (3653) and a 220-byte line limit (3636). Raising the baseline would weaken a guard the brief test exists to hold.

steps: Step 1, surveys.rs: add `check_behavior_test_design(reading) -> Result<()>`. Return Ok unless `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion(reading)`. Join all `code_surveys(reading)` text and take its `straight_lowercase`. (a) needs the phrase `entry point`; one of `gate order`, `order of the gates`, `order of gates`, `gates in order`, `gate sequence`; and one of `stop gate`, `stops at`, `stop at`, `must stop at`, `stops before`. The first identifier after the stop phrase (a token with `_`, `::` or `()`) must also appear earlier in the text, else the stop gate is not in the stated order. (b) needs `reuse`, `reuses`, `reused`, `reusing`, `extends` or `extending` followed within 8 tokens by an identifier, or the phrase `no existing function`. Both together contradict, and a reuse word with no identifier is missing. (c) needs one of: `names_record_evidence(survey)`, `names_record_kind` (a token `AnyRecord::<Name>` or `athena.<kind>/<n>`), or `no new output`/`no new record`. A survey that says `typed record` or `new record kind` with no kind token also needs a behavior criterion naming a round-trip identifier and at least one listed crates/ deliverable. (d) needs `direct check` or `directly`, plus `count`, `counts`, `counting` or `calls`. An unnegated skip-switch phrase (`skip switch`, `skip flag`, `test-only switch`, `--skip`) or internal-helper phrase (`internal helper`, `private helper`) in the survey or any criterion is a contradiction, and a `no`, `not`, `never` or `without` within 3 words before it cancels it. Collect every missing letter and contradiction into one `bail!` that starts 'the reading was refused because', names (a)-(d), and gives the template `Code survey: <paths>. Entry point: `f`. Gate order: `g1`, `g2`, `g3`. Stop gate: the test stops at `g2`. Reuses: `h`, or no existing function does this. Output: `AnyRecord::<Kind>` or no new output. Direct check: counts <planner/producer/model> calls on the fake, not a skip switch or a read of an internal helper.` Write the doc comment with the cause, the gate, the limits and the declared share.

demonstrations.method: The refusal-rule replay, in two parts. (1) A fixture replay test through `replay()`. (2) Athena's own replay at verification on the real records.
demonstrations.observes: (1) `design_check_replay_share_is_within_the_declared_range` builds 10 `ReplayCase` values shaped like recent accepted code readings: some with a short `Code survey:` only, some complete, some docs. The base checker is a closure that applies `refusing_check` and treats a refusal by `check_behavior_test_design` as accept, standing in for the build without the step. The candidate is `check_reading_text`. It runs `replay(&cases, &base, &candidate, replay_declaration_of(&reading).effective_share())` with the criterion text 'expected 20% of newly refused readings'. It asserts `!run.held` and `newly_refused.len() * 100 <= total * replay_limit_percent(Some(20))`, so the share is 25% or less.
